applies_why: The judge text labels Matthew 1:16 UNDERDETERMINED because the single verse admits both readings, which is the single-verse situation K-S2 governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. — I weighed whether a single verse admitting both readings is open/UNDERDETERMINED versus K-S2's command that it is not open and both senses stand.
why: The judge's UNDERDETERMINED rests on the single verse Matthew 1:16 admitting two readings, contrary to K-S2's command that such a verse is not open and both senses stand.
